newsitem.title: UK: Labour spokesman sees Scots parliament coalition.
newsitem.headline: Labour spokesman sees Scots parliament coalition.

text.p: Coalition government could become the norm in a Scottish parliament which Labour is committed to setting up if it wins the May 1 British election, the party's Scottish spokesman has said.

George Robertson said in an interview which appears in this week's edition of the New Statesman political weekly: "It's going to be difficult to govern without coalition in Scotland. A consensus will have to be established."

Labour has agreed to a proportional voting system for the Scottish and Welsh parliaments it is pledged to set up, and has also promised a referendum on whether a similar system should be used to elect the British parliament.
"Labour may be the first political party in the democratic world to give up its advantage in the current voting system," Robertson said.
He said he would be proud to serve in the first Scottish parliament, and predicted that the institution would "break the mindset that the only way to run a country is from Whitehall".
